title: Surface ink scale and component fallbacks for dark-mode brand preservation
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: During recent private tenant theming tests, brand accents and component tones look washed out or lose contrast in dark surfaces, particularly for dense UI controls (tables, tokenized lists) and embedded third-party charts. We need a deterministic mapping strategy that preserves perceived brand color and hierarchy while ensuring accessibility and predictable component behavior.

Goal: Define an "ink scale" approach and component fallback rules that map existing light-mode tokens to dark-mode equivalents in a way that: preserves brand hue and recognizability, maintains minimum contrast ratios for text/icons/interactive elements, and provides clear overrides for components that cannot rely solely on token mapping (eg. third-party charts, legacy buttons).

Scope: tokens (surface, ink, brand accents), core components (buttons, tables, code blocks, chips), charts (line/area/bar colors), and component-level overrides/fallbacks. Implementation will include design tokens, example component CSS/system tokens, and a rollout plan with canary routes in the Console.

Constraints: Must work with existing runtime theming API and Redwood token naming conventions; minimize API changes. Aim for deterministic, computed token outputs (token transforms) rather than manual per-brand themes when possible.

Risks: Over-adjusting brand hue in dark can change product recognition; too-aggressive saturation increases visual noise. Third-party chart libraries may require color remapping hooks or overlays.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical ink-scale spec (5–7 levels) exists that maps to light and dark surfaces with numeric token values and usage guidance
All core interactive components (primary/secondary/tertiary buttons, table rows, chips) render correctly with new tokens across sample brand colors without contrast failures (WCAG AA for normal text)
Chart color palette mapping documented with fallback rules for 3rd-party libs and an adapter pattern for Vega/Chart.js used in Console
Design system includes fallback component overrides for cases where token mapping is insufficient (example: legacy third-party widget) and a small set of CSS utility classes to opt into overrides
Figma spec and token export (JSON) checked into design-assets with example screens for three brand hues (blue, teal, magenta)
Rollout plan with canary route and monitoring hooks (token-level diff dashboard) approved and scheduled in console-2026.03
updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff sync with Platform Eng (Ravi Singh) and Frontend Eng (Noah Patel). Agreed to prioritize computed token transforms rather than per-brand manual files.

2026-02-18: Exploratory visual tests in Figma showing brand hue shift strategies: preserve hue vs preserve luminance. Design preference: preserve hue with controlled desaturation and contrast bump for surface anchors.
2026-02-20: Prototype ink-scale (IS-0 ... IS-6) created and exported as tokens. Shared PRD: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DS/pages/Ink+Scale+Spec

2026-02-22: Frontend eng provided implementation constraints: runtime only supports token transforms + per-theme overrides; agreed to implement a computed transform function in runtime that applies hue-preserving darken + contrast delta.

2026-02-24: Accessibility review with Emma Clark. Found one failing combo for small table actions in magenta brand at IS-1; proposed change to bump contrast for interactive icon color on low-surface contrast combos.

2026-02-26: Chart kit workshop: identified that Chart.js color arrays are passed directly; agreed to add a small adapter to map chart palette through theme token transforms. Created initial adapter RFC: GH PR #8210.
2026-02-28: Draft Figma screens uploaded (figma.com/file/rdw-ink-scale-demo) and export token JSON checked into design-assets/tokens/ink-scale-v1.json. Beginning implementation tickets for frontend.
Next: Implement runtime transform function ENG-73955, add chart adapter ENG-73956, and schedule canary in console-2026.03
notes: We should include a small visual test harness in Storybook demonstrating 3 brand hues and the fallback behavior for chart widgets. Consider adding a 'brand intensity' knob in the Console theme editor for customers to choose conservative or vivid mapping. Track changes with token-level diffs so we can revert if customers report brand regressions.
